We introduce TinyNet, a two-layer MLP for tabular classifica-
tion. We evaluate on the public UCI Adult dataset, available from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. The data is split 70/15/15 into train, validation and test sets with a fixed seed.

Inputs are standardized and rows with missing values are dropped. We train for 20 epochs with Adam, learning rate 0.001 and batch size 128 on a single NVIDIA T4 GPU. We compare against logistic regression and gradient boosted trees.

TinyNet reaches 85.1% test accuracy versus 84.2% for gradient boosted trees. Removing the second layer lowers accuracy to 83.0%. We report accuracy on the held-out test set, averaged over five seeds. Our study is limited to one dataset.
